title: Separate Field Scoring Protects Unused Tools When Agents Pool Tool-Use Experience
title_zh: 独立字段评分：当智能体共享工具使用经验时保护未使用工具

paragraphs.en: Agents that call tools from a shared catalog can pool what they learn about which tool serves which request. We measure what pooled usage examples do to tool retrieval, reporting separately the held-out tools, for which no agent has usage, and all other tools. Adding usage examples to the index as extra entries for used tools raises Hit@5 (whether a gold tool is in the top five) for those tools and lowers it for held-out tools, by a large margin on two of three catalogs and with both embedders we tested. Giving used tools the same number of equally long entries filled with other tools’ text lowers held-out Hit@5 about as much, but gives little or none of the gain. We call our method of scoring usage as its own field Synapse . On StableToolBench, the held-out gold tool appears in its top five more often than with a router that reserves slots for usage (0.785 against 0.683), and this held-out lead holds on all three catalogs with both embedders. This protection persisted when we replaced each tool’s usage with other tools’ text, and a constant score offset for tools with usage gives similar held-out Hit@5 in most settings. The gain for tools with usage, in contrast, needs usage about the right tool. The router keeps more of the gain on labeled queries on TOUCAN with both embedders and on ToolRet with one, so the better choice depends on the workload. Splitting the usage among ten simulated agents shows that pooling helps exactly as much as giving one agent the same records.
paragraphs.zh: 从共享目录调用工具的智能体可以汇集它们学到的知识，即哪个工具服务于哪个请求。 我们衡量汇集的使用样例对工具检索的影响，并分别报告留出工具（没有任何智能体使用过）和所有其他工具的结果。 将使用样例作为额外条目加入已使用工具的索引中，可以提高这些工具的 Hit@5（即正确工具是否排在前五名），但会大幅降低留出工具的 Hit@5，在三个目录中的两个上以及我们测试的两种嵌入器上均是如此。 给已使用工具配上相同数量的、填充其他工具文本的等长条目，也会使留出 Hit@5 降低大约同样的幅度，但几乎或完全不会带来增益。 我们将这种把使用情况作为独立字段进行评分的方法称为 Synapse。 在 StableToolBench 上，留出的正确工具排在前五名的频率高于为使用情况保留槽位的路由器（0.785 对 0.683），且在三种目录和两种嵌入器上，留出工具的这一优势均保持不变。 当我们把每个工具的使用文本替换为其他工具的文本时，这种保护仍然存在；在大多数设置中，给有使用记录的工具一个恒定的分数偏移也能得到相近的留出 Hit@5。 相比之下，有使用记录的工具所获得的增益需要关于该工具本身的使用记录。 路由器在 TOUCAN 上（两种嵌入器）以及 ToolRet 上（一种嵌入器）的带标注查询上保留了更多增益，因此更好的选择取决于工作负载。 将使用记录分配给十个模拟智能体的实验表明，汇集带来的帮助与让单个智能体拥有相同记录完全一样。

paragraphs.en: A user asks an agent to fetch every product from a Shopify store and return the full record of one item. The right tool, shopify_store_scraper , is in the catalog with its documentation, but no agent has used it yet. Suppose the agents that share this catalog pool their past usage and add each example to the retrieval index as an extra entry for its tool; we call this folding. A usage example is a past request labeled with the tool that served it. In our StableToolBench runs, the retriever’s five candidates for this request then no longer contain the scraper (query 10277, seed 42). With documentation alone, they do. We selected this query to show the failure, not to estimate how often it happens.

paragraphs.en: Tool-retrieval benchmarks do not report tools that have shared usage separately from tools that have none ( Qin et al. 2024 ; Shi et al. 2025 ) . Shared usage moves two groups of tools in opposite directions, and one average hides both moves. We fix a held-out set of tools for which no agent contributes usage (the unused tools of our title); their documentation stays in the catalog, and held-out says nothing about what the embedding model saw in pretraining. We call every other tool labeled; whether a labeled tool has usage depends on the seed and the catalog (for 88%, 21% and 97% of labeled queries on our three catalogs, every gold tool has usage). Our metric is Hit@5: whether a gold tool is among the five candidates passed to the agent. It measures retrieval only, not whether the agent then completes the task.
paragraphs.zh: 工具检索基准并未将具有共享使用情况的工具与没有共享使用情况的工具分开报告（Qin et al. 2024；Shi et al. 2025）。 共享使用情况使两组工具朝相反方向移动，而一个平均值掩盖了这两种移动。 我们固定了一组保留工具，没有任何智能体为其贡献使用记录（即标题中的“未使用工具”）；它们的文档仍保留在目录中，而“保留”并不意味着嵌入模型在预训练中是否见过它们。 我们将其余所有工具称为已标注工具；某个已标注工具是否具有使用记录取决于随机种子和目录（在我们的三个目录上，分别有 88%、21% 和 97% 的已标注查询中，每个黄金工具都有使用记录）。 我们的指标是 Hit@5：即某个黄金工具是否位于传给智能体的五个候选工具之中。 它只衡量检索效果，而不衡量智能体随后是否完成任务。

paragraphs.en: We compare three ways to combine usage with documentation. In folding, each usage entry is serialized together with its tool’s metadata, and a tool is scored by its best entry, documentation or usage. A two-index router reserves some of the five slots for a separate usage index. Synapse keeps usage as its own field. Each tool gets one score for its documentation and one for its best-matching usage example. Both scores are z-normalized across tools for the query, and one weight chosen on development data mixes them. A tool without usage keeps its documentation score.

paragraphs.en: We ask three questions. RQ1: who gains and who loses when usage is folded into the index? On StableToolBench and TOUCAN, folding lowers held-out Hit@5 by about 30 points and raises labeled Hit@5. On ToolRet both changes are small. Length-matched text from other tools causes a similar held-out loss on the two catalogs where we ran this control. RQ2: how should usage be combined? Synapse keeps more held-out Hit@5 than the router on all three catalogs. The router retrieves more labeled tools on TOUCAN with both embedders and on ToolRet with one, so neither method dominates. RQ3: does pooling across agents pay? Pooling the usage of ten simulated agents raises Hit@5 over the average single agent, mostly for labeled tools, and matches one agent holding all the records. On the workshop’s question of when a collective merely adds cost: when usage is folded into the index, the cost falls on tools nobody has used yet, and the combination rule decides how large it is.

paragraphs.en: On StableToolBench ( Guo et al. 2024 ) , the held-out set is the 172 gold tools of the G1-tool and G1-category groups. We first remove exact and near-duplicate (Jina cosine ≥ 0.95 \geq 0.95 ) copies of test queries from the usage pool. We then drop every record that labels a held-out tool or mentions its name, which leaves 90,704 records. Tools are hashed into development and test buckets. A held-out query has every gold tool in the held-out set, and a labeled query has none, so a held-out hit always means a held-out tool was retrieved. We exclude the 80 queries with gold tools in both sets and the 85 whose gold tools span development and test buckets, which leaves 161 held-out-test and 149 labeled-test queries. Three seeds supply three different client usage pools, each covering about 2,430 tools. We filter ToolRet ( Shi et al. 2025 ) to exclude its ToolBench, ToolBench-SAM, APIGen and ToolLens sources. It then has 26,423 tools, 255 held-out-test and 728 labeled-test queries, and at most eight usage entries per tool. On ToolRet and on the TOUCAN-derived catalog ( Xu et al. 2025 ) (2,159 tools; 769 held-out-test and 2,595 labeled-test queries), there are no benchmark groups to hold out, so a salted SHA-256 hash of the tool identifier sends 30% of tools to the held-out set (7,905 and 627 tools) and a second hash assigns development and test. Queries whose gold tools disagree on either assignment are excluded, as on StableToolBench. Pooled over seeds, every gold tool has usage for 88% of labeled-test queries on StableToolBench, 21% on ToolRet and 97% on TOUCAN (Appendix A).

paragraphs.en: To test whether the loss depends on what the usage says, we keep every tool’s identifier, documentation and number of usage entries, and replace each entry with text from other tools of exactly the same tokenizer length (Figure 2 ). Held-out Hit@5 stays within about two points of the real-usage value on both catalogs, and both intervals include zero. Labeled-test Hit@5 falls by 33 and 27 points. With Nomic on StableToolBench, the pattern repeats: held-out Hit@5 with other tools’ text is 1.86 points above real usage ([ − 1.24 -1.24 , 5.10]), and labeled Hit@5 is 12.75 points below it. The labeled gain needs text about the right tool. The held-out loss does not, since other tools’ text of the same length is about as harmful. The control keeps both the number of entries per tool and their length, so it cannot tell whether the loss comes from extra entries (more chances for a used tool to score high) or from longer text. Limiting folding to one usage entry per used tool shrinks the held-out loss but does not remove it: held-out Hit@5 stays below documentation-only on every catalog with both embedders, for example 0.553 against 0.733 on StableToolBench with Jina (Appendix I). Used tools then still have two entries and other tools one. The control does not separate length from generic query-like style or from competition within one index, and it does not show the two conditions are equivalent. A few donor entries share a gold label with their target; Appendix E reports and keeps them.
paragraphs.zh: 为了检验这一损失是否取决于使用条目的内容，我们保留每个工具的标识符、文档以及使用条目的数量，并将每一条使用文本替换为分词后长度完全相同的其他工具的文本（图 2）。 在两个工具目录上，留出测试的 Hit@5 与真实使用条件下的差距保持在约两个百分点以内，且两个置信区间都包含零。 标注测试集上的 Hit@5 分别下降了 33 和 27 个百分点。 在 StableToolBench 上使用 Nomic 时，该模式再次出现：使用其他工具文本时留出测试的 Hit@5 比真实使用高 1.86 个百分点（[−1.24, 5.10]），而标注测试的 Hit@5 则低 12.75 个百分点。 标注测试带来的收益需要关于正确工具的文本。 留出测试造成的损失则不需要，因为其他工具的等长文本造成了大致相同的危害。 该对照实验同时保留了每个工具的条目数量和文本长度，因此无法区分损失究竟来自额外增加的条目（使被使用工具获得高分的机会更多），还是来自更长的文本。 将折叠限制为每个被使用工具仅一条使用条目可以缩小留出测试损失，但无法消除它：在两个嵌入模型和所有工具目录上，留出测试的 Hit@5 仍低于仅使用文档的条件，例如在 StableToolBench 上使用 Jina 时为 0.553 对 0.733（附录 I）。 此时被使用工具仍拥有两条使用条目，而其他工具只有一条。 该对照实验既未将文本长度与泛化的查询式风格区分开，也未将其与同一索引内的竞争区分开，且并未证明两种条件是等价的。 少数供体条目与其目标工具共享同一金标准标签；附录 E 对其进行了报告并予以保留。

paragraphs.en: Two controls separate how Synapse scores usage from what the usage says (Appendix I). First, we add one constant, tuned on development data, to the documentation score of every tool with usage. paragraphs.en: We split StableToolBench’s fixed usage pool among 1, 2, 5 or 10 simulated agents by hashing each source query, and score with the frozen Synapse weight (Figure 4 ). paragraphs.en: Tool retrievers select from documentation ( Qin et al. 2024 ) , and off-the-shelf retrievers find tool retrieval hard ( Shi et al. 2025 ) . Expanding documents with predicted queries helps the documents that receive the expansion ( Nogueira et al. 2019 ) . Tool2Vec represents each tool by the average embedding of the queries that used it ( Moon et al. 2024 ) , and Tool-Embed is trained on LLM-expanded tool documentation ( Lu et al. 2026 ) . Re-Invoke expands every tool with generated queries ( Chen et al. 2024 ) . These works measure what expansion does to the tools that receive it; Lu et al. (2026) also find that example-usage fields help least and longer documents lower similarity. We study the tools left without expansion when they compete with expanded ones: our folding arm expands used tools only, and our length control suggests that the cost falls on the tools left out. Scoring fields separately is an old idea in retrieval ( Robertson et al. 2004 ; Li et al. 2025 ) . We use a simple form of it and measure which tools it protects. Federated agent learning shares free-text knowledge or in-context examples across clients ( Wu et al. 2024 ; Wang et al. 2025 ) or federates router parameters ( Askin et al. 2026 ) .

paragraphs.en: All results are retrieval Hit@5 with two embedders; our audit of Nomic’s training data is incomplete, so we make no contamination-free claim for it. We have not tested task success, a tool-trained retriever such as Tool-Embed, or Re-Invoke, and make no claim about them. Agents are simulated partitions of one usage pool, and no privacy mechanism is applied. The length control ran on two catalogs and does not separate token length from query-like style or index competition, and our entry-budget control still gives used tools one more entry than other tools. paragraphs.en: Shared usage helps the tools it describes and, when folded into one index, can push tools nobody has used out of the candidate list. paragraphs.en: Hit@5 gives credit when any gold tool is among five distinct candidates; on single-gold queries it equals Recall@5. paragraphs.en: Each usage entry keeps its tool, documentation, field labels and entry count, and its text is replaced by text from other tools in the same pool with exactly the same untruncated Jina-tokenizer length. All 113,110 StableToolBench entries (the usage entries of the three seed pools, 37,414, 38,008 and 37,688, each drawn from the 90,704 filtered source records) and all 6,617 TOUCAN entries pass this check. On StableToolBench, 704 entries (0.62%) have a donor whose gold labels include the target and 411 (0.36%) keep identical text; on TOUCAN the counts are 408 (6.17%) and 391 (5.91%). Three TOUCAN entries per seed exceed the encoder’s 8,192-token limit and are truncated the same way in the real and control conditions.

paragraphs.en: Table 7 gives Hit@5 with Nomic Embed v1.5 (136.7M parameters, 8,192-token context) at the settings selected on development tools for this embedder. Selection used the same 11 weights and four quotas, with the objective of mean held-out and labeled development Hit@5 over three seeds; development and test gold tools are disjoint. On StableToolBench the selected settings equal Jina’s. Carrying Jina’s settings over unchanged gives the same router results and Synapse results within 1.3 points of these. The Nomic length control matches lengths with Nomic’s own tokenizer, over the full serialized input including its task prefix; all 113,110 entries match and none is truncated. The audit of Nomic’s public training data for exposure to these benchmarks is not complete.
paragraphs.zh: 表 7 给出了 Nomic Embed v1.5（1.367 亿参数，8192 词元上下文）在针对该嵌入器于开发工具上选定的设置下的 Hit@5。 选择使用了同样的 11 个权重和四个配额，目标是在三个随机种子上的平均留出与开发集 Hit@5；开发集与测试集的金标准工具互不相交。 在 StableToolBench 上，选定的设置与 Jina 的相同。 将 Jina 的设置原样沿用，得到的路由器结果相同，且 Synapse 结果与这些结果相差在 1.3 分以内。 Nomic 的长度控制使用 Nomic 自身的分词器，对包含任务前缀在内的完整序列化输入进行长度匹配；全部 113,110 条条目均匹配且无一被截断。 针对 Nomic 公开训练数据是否涉及这些基准的审计尚未完成。

paragraphs.en: On StableToolBench, Synapse gains 4.30 points of Hit@5 ([1.29, 7.45]) at the observed mix of 161 held-out and 149 labeled test queries (48.1% labeled). Synapse is better when fewer than 83.4% of queries go to labeled tools (interval [59.2%, 100%]). If a labeled query must have usage for every gold tool, the cutoff is 78.4% ([55.3%, 100%]). An upper endpoint of 100% includes bootstrap draws with no crossing, so above about 59% the data do not decide. These cutoffs assume that each stratum’s Hit@5 carries over to the target workload, and we did not compute them for ToolRet or TOUCAN.
paragraphs.zh: 在 StableToolBench 上，在由 161 个保留测试查询和 149 个已标注测试查询组成的观测混合比例（48.1% 已标注）下，Synapse 的 Hit@5 提升 4.30 分（[1.29, 7.45]）。 当去往已标注工具的查询少于 83.4% 时（区间 [59.2%, 100%]），Synapse 表现更好。 如果要求已标注查询对每个金标工具都有使用记录，则临界值为 78.4%（[55.3%, 100%]）。 上端点为 100% 意味着自举抽样中存在无交叉的情况，因此在约 59% 以上时数据无法给出定论。 这些临界值假设每个分层的 Hit@5 可以迁移到目标工作负载，并且我们没有为 ToolRet 或 TOUCAN 计算它们。

paragraphs.en: Over 340 labeled StableToolBench queries, development queries included, the usage-minus-documentation score separates gold tools from distractor labeled tools at the same documentation rank with an AUC of 0.817 ([0.780, 0.850]). This is consistent with usage pushing unrelated labeled tools down, but it is a pooled diagnostic, not a test-only result.
paragraphs.zh: 在超过340个带标注的StableToolBench查询（含开发查询）上，使用度减去文档度的分数在相同文档排名下区分黄金工具与带标注的干扰工具，AUC为0.817（[0.780, 0.850]）。 这与使用度将无关的带标注工具排挤下去相一致，但它是一个汇总的诊断指标，并非仅用测试集得到的结果。

sents.zh: 在超过340个带标注的StableToolBench查询（含开发查询）上，使用度减去文档度的分数在相同文档排名下区分黄金工具与带标注的干扰工具，AUC为0.817（[0.780, 0.850]）。

paragraphs.en: All three controls reuse the cached embeddings, splits and three seeds, and reproduce every baseline candidate list exactly before scoring. The fixed entry budget keeps exactly one usage entry per used tool, chosen by a query-independent content hash, plus one documentation entry per tool; tools without usage keep only documentation. The offset control adds a constant β \beta to the standardized documentation score of every tool with usage, with β ∈ { 0 , ± 0.25 , ± 0.5 , … , ± 2 , ± 2.5 , ± 3 } \beta\in\{0,\pm 0.25,\pm 0.5,\ldots,\pm 2,\pm 2.5,\pm 3\} selected on development data (selected values: StableToolBench − 0.25 -0.25 with Jina and − 0.5 -0.5 with Nomic; ToolRet + 0.5 +0.5 with both; TOUCAN − 0.25 -0.25 with Jina and + 0.5 +0.5 with Nomic). The other-tool control permutes the complete set of usage texts and vectors across tools so that no tool keeps its own; entry counts and the global length distribution are kept, but per-entry length is not matched. We report it at each setting’s frozen Synapse weight. All results are descriptive on test sets seen in earlier work.
paragraphs.zh: 三项对照全部复用缓存的嵌入、切分和三个随机种子，并在打分前完全复现每个基线候选列表。 固定的条目预算为每个被使用的工具保留恰好一条使用记录条目（由与查询无关的内容哈希选定），外加每个工具一条文档条目；没有使用记录的工具只保留文档条目。 偏移对照为每个有使用记录的工具的标准化文档分数加上一个常数 β \beta，其中 β ∈ { 0 , ± 0.25 , ± 0.5 , … , ± 2 , ± 2.5 , ± 3 } \beta\in\{0,\pm 0.25,\pm 0.5,\ldots,\pm 2,\pm 2.5,\pm 3\} 在开发数据上选定（选定值：StableToolBench 在 Jina 下为 − 0.25 -0.25，在 Nomic 下为 − 0.5 -0.5；ToolRet 在两者下均为 + 0.5 +0.5；TOUCAN 在 Jina 下为 − 0.25 -0.25，在 Nomic 下为 + 0.5 +0.5）。 他工具对照将全部使用文本和向量在各工具之间进行置换，使得没有任何工具保留自己的使用记录；条目数量和全局长度分布得以保留，但不匹配每条记录的长度。 我们在每个设定冻结的 Synapse 权重处报告该结果。 所有结果都是在先前工作中已见过的测试集上的描述性结果。

sents.en: Against documentation-only, the one-entry folded arm lowers held-out Hit@5 by 18.01 ([12.80, 23.33]), 1.57 ([0.38, 3.19]) and 19.98 ([10.93, 28.82]) points with Jina on StableToolBench, ToolRet and TOUCAN, and by 9.52 ([4.60, 15.40]), 1.70 ([0.39, 3.40]) and 13.78 ([7.94, 19.75]) points with Nomic.
sents.zh: 相对于仅文档基线，单条目折叠式臂在 StableToolBench、ToolRet 和 TOUCAN 上使用 Jina 时，使留出集 Hit@5 分别下降 18.01（[12.80, 23.33]）、1.57（[0.38, 3.19]）和 19.98（[10.93, 28.82]）个点；使用 Nomic 时分别下降 9.52（[4.60, 15.40]）、1.70（[0.39, 3.40]）和 13.78（[7.94, 19.75]）个点。
